datasheet.title: Juniper QFX5240 line of Switches datasheet (a00150802ENW, Rev. 2, March 2026)

description: Juniper QFX5240-64OD, a 2RU 800G data-centre spine switch running Junos OS Evolved. It has 64 OSFP ports (800 GbE) in sixteen columns of four, in four groups of four columns, and two SFP+ ports (10 GbE), with a lamp beside each network port. The port side also carries the RJ-45 management, console and time-of-day ports, a USB port, the reset button, the three chassis lamps, the 1 PPS and 10 MHz connectors. The rear carries two 3000 W AC power supplies stacked at the left and four front-to-back fan modules. It ships as one front panel in one AC airflow-out build, and as a spare chassis with no supplies and no fan modules. Its sibling with QSFP-DD cages is the QFX5240-64QD.

gaps.wanted: The depth and the registry size of the OSFP cage. The library's std/osfp has no registry entry and carries an estimated depth; the 23.1 by 13.5 mm opening it uses was measured on another maker's 2RU box and the photograph here agrees with it.
The depth of the fan module and of the power supplies. The guide's figures 15, 16, 18 and 19 carry no scale and its tables state weights only for the whole chassis.

The chassis width. The datasheet's Table 2 says 17.26 in (43.8 cm); the guide's Table 7 says 19.03 in (48.33 cm), which is 17.26 in plus the front brackets (the rack-requirements table states 19 in over the brackets). The datasheet's 17.26 in is used because the photograph's scale is consistent with it; the depth differs by 0.01 in (25.52 against 25.51), and the datasheet's is used.
The maximum power of the QFX5240-64OD. Guide Table 13 says 2198 W; the datasheet says 2116 W. Same measure and same scope (maximum, 40 C, IMIX traffic). The guide's 2198 W is used.

The AC input of the supply. Guide Table 4 says 200 to 240 VAC at 16 A maximum; guide Table 13 says an operating range of 200 to 277 VAC and 6 A at 200 VAC, 3.8 A at 240 VAC; the datasheet says 180 to 264 VAC. Table 4's range is carried on the supply and every reading is kept in the device's `power-input-ac`.
The type of the two small cages. The guide's callout 2 calls them "SFP28 ports" and its text and the datasheet call them "2 x 10-Gbps SFP+ ports". They are modelled as SFP+ at 10 Gbps.

Which ports take high power optics. The guide's note says that only the front-panel ports in the middle rows support them and lists 1, 2, 5, 6, 9, 10 and so on to 61 and 62, which are ports of the second and third rows in a column of four, counting from 0. The note is carried in `features.optics-osfp` and the face does not mark those ports, because the metal does not.

The DC supply. The datasheet's ordering table lists QFX5241-PWR-DC-AO as "QFX5240 Series-2RU DC PSU, Air Out"; the QFX5240 hardware guide describes AC supplies only and no photograph of a DC build is held.

The lamps of the management jack. Guide figure 14 and Table 10 describe lamps on the management port; the photograph shows them at the corners of the upper jack. The jack is drawn with the library's lamped jack.

The connector type of the 1PPS and 10MHz jacks. The guide calls them "clock input and output connectors"; the photograph shows gold coaxial jacks 6 mm across, drawn as the library's SMA jack. Estimated.
The rating label of each supply and the serial number labels (figures 45 to 48). Not drawn.
The rack ears' positions and the rack kit's contract. The guide names QFX5240-2U-4PRMK and no kit contract exists in the library; none is written here.

attrs.redundancy-note: QFX5240 hardware guide, Component Redundancy: four fan modules of two rotors each, N+1 redundancy at rotor level; the fan modules are hot-insertable and hot-removable

grounding.description: the protective earthing terminal, a pad with two M6 studs at the left of the rear (guide, Ground the QFX5240 Switch)

mgmt.mixed: the out-of-band cluster at the right of the port side - an RJ-45 console port, an RJ-45 management port, an RJ-45 time-of-day port, a USB port and the recessed reset button. Five kinds, one purpose: reaching, timing and recovering the switch when the data plane cannot.

osfp-leds.description: One RGB lamp per network port, in the strip above the upper band and below the lower band (guide Table 8).

attrs.redundancy-note: two supplies, 1+1; hot-removable and hot-insertable without shutting the switch down (guide, Component Redundancy)

sfp-plus.description: Ports 64 and 65 as printed, rel-pos carrying the printed number, since the origin token cannot express a block that starts at 64.

status-leds.description: The three chassis lamps ID, SYS and ALM (guide Table 9).

timing.description: the 1 PPS and 10 MHz connectors, a pair of coaxial jacks for the switch's timing references

name: qfx5240-64od

chassis.note: datasheet Table 2: 17.26 x 3.46 x 25.52 in (43.8 x 8.8 x 64.8 cm), 2RU, 22 kg (48.50 lb) fully loaded without optics. The inch figures are used. The guide's Table 7 prints the same height and weight and a width of 19.03 in (48.33 cm) and a depth of 25.51 in (65 cm); 19.03 in is the width over the front brackets, which is the rack-face width the datasheet's 17.26 in leaves out, so the datasheet's body width is used and brackets are not modelled. The depth differs by 0.01 in; the datasheet's 25.52 in is used.

colour.note: The front plate samples #6e7784 (a bare patch near the left edge) and the rear panel #646d79. The chassis colour is the front's. The photographs are lit warmly and these are their values, not a paint reference.

drawing-vs-photo.note: The guide's figures 2 and 3 are the same studio photographs at reduced size and agree with them. The guide calls the SFP pair "SFP28 ports" in its callouts and the text and the datasheet say SFP+ 10 GbE; the group is stated at 10g. The photograph shows the supplies' hubs carrying the supply maker's name; it is a third party's logo and is not drawn.

ears-and-kits.note: NOT MODELLED. The guide names the rack mount kit QFX5240-2U-4PRMK (a four-post tool-less kit, Table 6 and the datasheet's ordering table). The library holds no contract for it and none is written here, so `chassis.ears` and `chassis.kits` are left out and a gap says so. The modelled body is the 438.4 mm chassis, without brackets.

earthing.note: Two threaded studs 15.5 mm apart on a pad at the left of the rear, under the ground symbol, 6.4 mm from the left edge. The guide's grounding section (figure 1 and Ground the QFX5240 Switch) calls for two M6 screws with star washers and a Panduit LCDXN2-14AF-E lug, which is a two-hole lug on 5/8 in centres; the 15.5 mm pitch of the photograph agrees. The guide's text puts the terminal "on the side of the chassis" and "through the left-front mounting bracket"; the photograph and the guide's figure 1 show it on the rear panel, and the photograph is followed.

front-green-tab.note: The green tab at the foot of the management panel, 17.0 mm wide and 2.7 mm tall, is the chassis serial number pull-out (callout 8 of figure 6). It is drawn as decor, because it is a label card and not a part the library models.

gate-1.note: The front photograph's body, between the left and right edges, is 1929 px wide and 391 px from the top edge to the bottom lip, an aspect of 4.93 against the datasheet's 438.4 / 87.9 = 4.99 (1.2 percent out). Scale 4.40 px/mm across, used on both axes with the origin at the left edge (x 82 px) and the top edge (y 154 px). The rear photograph's body is 1895 px wide, 4.323 px/mm. The guide's figures 2 to 5 are half-tone thumbnails and are used only to count and read.

lifecycle.note: Searched for an end-of-life announcement. The guide, published 2026-07-10, and the datasheet, March 2026, state none and no Juniper notice was found in the intake. The device states none announced. Estimated, because absence in the documents is not a notice from the maker.

logo.note: The maker's logo and its lockup are printed at the upper right of the face, above the model name QFX5240-64OD. The logo is not drawn: a logo-zone region is reserved where it stands, and the model name is drawn as plain text.

mgmt-panel.note: Right of the last group, from the top: the model name under the maker's logo, the RJ-45 management port with a USB-A port under it in one shield (MGMT, and the USB 3 symbol), the stacked SFP+ pair with 64 and 65 below it, a strip with the legends ID, SYS and ALM above three lamps and the RST pinhole, the 1PPS and 10MHz coaxial jacks, the RJ-45 console (CON) and time-of-day (TOD) jacks stacked in one shield, and a green serial-number tab at the foot (guide figure 6 callouts 1 to 9). The panel stands where the QFX5240-64QD's does, within 1 mm in the two photographs. The USB tongue is blue in the photograph, which is the USB-IF colour of a 3.0 port; the guide says "USB port" only.

modules.note: The four fan modules (QFX5240-2U-FANAO) and the two power supplies (QFX5240-PWR-AC-AO) are field-replaceable units in bays, each its own component (guide Table 6). Nothing on this chassis is a built-in unit that is not a bay. Each supply carries its own small fan inside.

port-lamps.note: Each network port has a single RGB lamp (guide, QFX5240 Network Port LEDs, Table 8): in the photograph two dots 2.0 mm across between the two numerals of a column, above the upper band for ports 4c and 4c+1 and below the lower band for ports 4c+2 and 4c+3, read at 9.8 and 13.6 mm from the left edge of the column (estimated to 0.4 mm) and drawn at 9.5 and 13.9 mm, 2.05 mm either side of the cage's centre, so that a lamp is plainly not trying to centre on its cage. The lamps are unlit. The SFP+ ports show no lamp and the guide describes none.

port-numbering.note: Printed on a strip above the upper band and a strip below the lower band, read off the photograph: over each column "N up-arrow ... down-arrow N+1" with N a multiple of four, and under each column the same with N+2. So a column holds ports 4c to 4c+3 from the top, the upper band's pair first; the SFP+ pair prints "64 up-arrow" and "down-arrow 65" under it. Interface names are not printed and none is stated in the guide, so they are not recorded.

ports.note: Front photograph: 64 OSFP openings, sixteen columns of four in four groups of four columns. The cages abut inside a group on a 23.1 mm pitch (the library's OSFP cage, itself measured on another 2RU box with the same sixteen columns and four rows) and a group is 92.4 mm wide; the groups stand on a 97.1 mm pitch, 4.7 mm apart. The first cage starts at 8.3 mm. A column holds two rows in each of two bands (figures 2 and 6). The two SFP+ cages stand to the right of the last group, stacked, one above the other (callout 2, 14.5 mm wide).

power.note: Guide Table 13: typical 613 W and maximum 2198 W at 220 to 240 V for the QFX5240-64OD. The datasheet's power table says typical 613 W and maximum 2116 W (maximum measured at 40 C with DR optics, typical at 25 C with DACs at 50 percent load, excluding transceivers). The maxima differ (2198 and 2116 W); the guide's is used. AC input: guide Table 4 says 200 to 240 VAC at 16 A maximum, guide Table 13 says 200 to 277 VAC with 6 A at 200 VAC and 3.8 A at 240 VAC, and the datasheet says 180 to 264 VAC.

rear-layout.note: Rear photograph at 4.323 px/mm, checked against the guide's figure 3: two supplies stacked at the left end, supply 0 above supply 1, an earthing pad with two studs and the ground symbol under them, then four fan modules numbered 0 to 3 from the left on an 85.7 mm pitch. A fan symbol, the module number and an arrow are printed beside each fan opening, and a power symbol with the supply number beside each supply. The fan plates measure 80.3 mm wide and 80.0 mm high; the supplies 73.7 mm wide and 39.5 mm high.

row-pitch.note: The rows start at 11.4, 26.1, 47.4 and 62.2 mm from the top: 14.7 mm apart in the upper band and 14.8 mm in the lower, the openings 13.5 mm tall with a thin metal bar between the two rows of a band. The two bands are centred about the chassis centre.

sources.note: QFX5240 Switch Hardware Guide, published 2026-07-10, 147 pages (Juniper Networks, copyright 2026), from https://www.juniper.net/documentation/us/en/hardware/qfx5240/qfx5240.pdf: the front and rear figures 2 to 5, the port panel figures 6 to 13 and Tables 8 and 9 (lamps), Table 3 (hardware models), Tables 4 to 6 and 13 (power and cooling) and Table 7 (physical specifications). The QFX5240 line of Switches datasheet, a00150802ENW Rev. 2, 12 pages (Juniper Networks, published 2026-03; HPE document), from https://www.hpe.com/psnow/doc/a00150802enw: Table 2 (system capacity and dimensions), the power table and the ordering information. Juniper's studio photographs of the 64OD, front and rear (qfx5240-64od-front-high.jpg, 2100 x 706 px, and qfx5240-64od-rear-high.jpg, 2100 x 692 px, from juniper.net's image library). The documents and the photographs are the maker's and public; the guide and datasheet carry a copyright notice and no terms of use beyond it, so only facts are transcribed. No Visio stencil, 3D model or mechanical drawing is held for the QFX5240. The guide's figures are half-tone thumbnails of the same photographs.

variants.note: Guide Table 3 and datasheet ordering information: QFX5240-64OD-AO (AC, airflow out) and the spare QFX5240-64OD-CHAS, "Spare chassis without PSU and fans". Both share this front panel and the rear bays, so each is a configuration of this device. NOT MODELLED: the QFX5241-64OD (-AO, -DO, -DO-T2, -CHAS, -TCHAS), a sibling the guide's note and the datasheet name with its own part numbers and a DC supply, which has its own hardware guide and is left to its own slice; and the DC supply the datasheet lists for the series (QFX5241-PWR-DC-AO), which the QFX5240 guide does not describe.

vents.note: Hexagonal holes in the sheet: a band along the top above the cages, a band along the bottom, a column at the left edge, a column at the right edge and a field under the clock connectors. Drawn as vent decor in those positions, pitched to the photograph and estimated.
